title: The same spiral shell forms recur across unrelated groups, all ages and all seas

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The same spiral shell forms recur across unrelated groups, all ages and all seas

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Spiral shell forms appear with little relation to the kind of animal producing them, recurring in gastropods, cephalopods, foraminifera and tube worms, and mathematically identical forms recur in every geological period and are found mixed together regardless of climate or local conditions.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Again, we find the same forms, or forms which (save for external ornament) are mathematically identical, repeating themselves in all periods of the world’s geological history; and, irrespective of climate or local conditions, we see them mixed up, one with another, in the depths and on the shores of every sea.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XI, “The Logarithmic Spiral”; topic “Shell forms and Natural Selection”. Scope: spiral shells of molluscs, foraminifera and tube-dwelling worms through geological time

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch11-22: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.73

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Large open fossil, occurrence and morphology resources address all major variables. They can test recurrence and environmental association broadly, but harmonization and severe sampling biases prevent literal resolution of the universal scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Parameterize spiral shell form across molluscs, foraminifera and tube worms, then model recurrence and convergence against phylogeny, geological age, climate, depth and geography. The claim predicts frequent cross-group near-identity and weak environmental or temporal structure.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Preservation and collecting biases vary strongly through time and habitat.

Claims about 'every' period and sea exceed actual coverage.

Morphology and occurrence databases require substantial taxonomic linkage.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Occurrences through time and shell images are both public, so recurrence of coiled forms among molluscs, and their mixing in faunas, can be tested now. Extending mathematically identical to foraminifera and tube worms, in every period and irrespective of climate, needs a harmonized morphospace that only partly exists. That is months of alignment rather than a single standard analysis, and it would still leave sampling bias in the fossil record.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Place gastropod, cephalopod, foraminiferal and tube-worm shells in one coiling morphospace and test recurrence of the same forms across clades, geological periods and climate or depth settings. Repeated overlap, with forms mixed within deposits, supports the claim; forms restricted to clade, era or climate refute the corresponding part.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A common measurement protocol for molluscs, foraminifera and worm tubes is not already computed, and worm tubes are sparsely scanned.

Preservation and sampling differ by period and climate, which can create false recurrences or hide real habitat limits.
